title: Frontend Jest test quarantine adapter and execution flow
answers: How does test quarantine work in frontend Jest tests?
How does Jest handle flaky tests listed in .test_quarantine.json?
How to test changes to frontend/jest.quarantine.ts?
body:
PostHog isolates flaky Jest tests using a runner adapter configured during Jest bootstrap:
1. Rule parsing: `frontend/jest.quarantine.ts:parseQuarantine` reads `.test_quarantine.json` adhering to the contract defined in `tools/hogli-commands/hogli_commands/quarantine/core.py`.
2. Matching: `frontend/jest.quarantine.ts:activeJestEntries` filters entries for `runner: "jest"` valid on the current date, matching test IDs formatted as `<repo-relative-file>::<full test name>`.
3. Runtime interception: `frontend/jest.quarantine.ts:tolerateProvidesWhen` wraps test bodies (`it`, `test`) to catch failures, log `[quarantine] tolerated failure`, and prevent Jest from exiting non-zero.
4. Verification: The quarantine adapter is tested via spawned subprocesses in `frontend/src/test/jest.quarantine.test.ts` running against fixture file `frontend/src/test/jest.quarantine.runtime.fixture.ts`.
says: Known unstable frontend tests are still breaking continuous integration pull request checks
Tolerate previously reported flaky tests so releases are not blocked unnecessarily
Quarantined web interface tests still report failure instead of continuing the build
Automated test pipeline should safely ignore quarantined test failures
